report.humanness_verdict: Genuinely human at the sentence level, and noticeably more alive than a scripted reflector — but with visible seams a frequent returning user would start to feel. Averaged humanness is 4.0/5. The wins are real and not cosmetic: the 'I'm learning / I'm holding' register produces actual discovery moments that users name as such ('oh. yeah. thats it actually'), warmth and sign-offs vary and even charm ('may the mp3 mission go smoothly', 'Go be with your kid, and let the rest wait its turn'), corrections are humble and ego-free, and the old robotic crutches ('centre of this', quote-first openers, em-dashes) are essentially gone. What keeps it from a 5 is structural repetition the deterministic suppressor no longer catches: the 'is it more X, or Y?' option-menu has become the companion's reflexive move for narrowing a shade and recurs across 7 of 9 families, and softer stems ('That sounds like...' ~12-22% of turns depending on family, 'I'm learning this can feel like...') cluster in the early beats before the writing loosens. None of these breaks the voice in a single conversation, but they are exactly the kind of frame a daily user would begin to clock. The honest read: this feels like a small being most of the time, and like a well-built form roughly one turn in five.
report.usefulness_verdict: High and well-matched to the app's actual job, which is not to advise but to help a person find and own the shape of a feeling and then let it rest. Averaged usefulness is 4.78/5. The strongest evidence is that users repeatedly report the payoff unprompted ('more useful than I expected', 'helped more than a garage cleanout had any right to', 'feels a tiny bit less huge now', 'thank you for not trying to fix it'), and the app holds its hardest line under pressure: across every health-scare and medical-fear thread it gives zero advice and zero false reassurance while still feeling warm — that restraint is the product. The usefulness ceiling is set by two things. First, when a 'first shape' misfires (premature in flat__07, surface-level in shame__04) the user feels the let-down directly, so unlock timing is a usefulness lever, not just a UX nicety. Second, the safety-sequencing bug actively subtracts usefulness for the 3 sadness threads that never reached a first shape because they detoured into a harm-screen — those users left without the discovery the app exists to deliver. Fix the unlock-on-thin-material and the safety-ordering issues and usefulness is at the ceiling; everything else here is additive.

recommendations.title: Force a reflection before any gentle safety-check, and never re-fire the check verbatim
recommendations.problem: The level-2 gentle clarifier can be the companion's turn-1 line with no attunement before it (sadness__02), and the identical harm-screen can fire twice in one conversation after the user already answered (sadness__02 repeatedReply=1). Leading with a self-harm question on a soft opener, or re-asking after a plain 'no', reads as a tripwire, breaks trust on contact, and is the direct cause of sadness having the lowest unlock rate (3 threads never reach a first shape).
recommendations.change: In safetyClassifier.ts, split the level-2 response into two beats: (a) require a brief mirror/reflection of the user's actual words to be emitted first, then (b) the clarifier. Gate the clarifier so it cannot be the literal turn-1 output when no reflection precedes it. Add a per-conversation 'gentle-check already asked + answered' flag so the verbatim screen cannot re-fire once the user has given a non-crisis answer; on a second ambiguous cue, vary the wording and reference the prior answer ('earlier you said it was more tired than unsafe — is that still where it is?'). Also respect an explicit exit cue (sadness__03 'gonna go'): if the user is mid-exit and the cue is ambiguous (not explicit ideation), prefer a soft single-line check-in over the full binary screen.
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/safetyClassifier.ts (level-2 deterministic clarifier + new answered-flag), with the turn-ordering enforced in src/services/ai/openaiClient.ts so the reflection precedes the screen.

recommendations.title: Stop pairing a mood label with the self-harm question inside one forced binary
recommendations.problem: All gentle-checks use one rigid either/or that puts a feeling-label ('completely worn down and fed up') and a crisis question ('thoughts of harming yourself') as the two poles of a single sentence. This is conceptually clumsy, is the one clearly templated line in the whole corpus (byte-identical across sadness/shame/hurt/fear/flat, gentleCheck totals 16), and forces a distressed person to self-sort into a binary that conflates two different registers.
recommendations.change: Rewrite the level-2 clarifier so the care question stands on its own rather than as the second option of a mood binary: lead with brief validation, then ask the safety question plainly and singly ('That sounds heavy. I want to check gently — are you feeling safe right now?'), keeping the 'either answer is okay to say here' permission. Keep this as a small set of 2-3 vetted variants (safety wording should stay tested, not improvised) so it is no longer one byte-identical string, but decouple the mood word from the crisis poll.

recommendations.title: Extend the scaffold suppressor to catch the 3-option / tailored 'is it more X, or Y?' menu
recommendations.problem: responsePolicy.ts successfully killed 'centre of this' and quote-first openers, but the model has drifted to a new crutch the detector misses: the option-menu in its three-option and freshly-worded forms. It is now the most repeated shape in the corpus (7 of 9 families) while eitherOr reads 0 everywhere, so the automated guard is blind to the exact thing reviewers flag as the top humanness dent.
recommendations.change: Broaden the either-or detector beyond the literal two-option form: match the underlying shape — an interrogative offering a comma/'or'-separated list of 2+ emotion/quality words as choices ('more A, B, or something else?', 'more X or Y?', 'did it land more like A or B?'). When detected, either rewrite to a single open question ('what word feels closest?') or suppress and let the reflection rest. Cap the option-menu to at most once per conversation so it stays a tool, not a reflex. Pair this with a one-line guidance change in prompts.ts: 'Prefer one open question that hands the user the naming; do not present a menu of emotion words to choose from, especially before they have offered their own.'
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/responsePolicy.ts (generalize the eitherOr matcher + frequency cap) and src/services/ai/prompts.ts (question-generation guidance).

recommendations.title: Gate the shade (not just the family) to the user's actual word before it can be stored
recommendations.problem: stage.ts labelIsUserOwned() correctly enforces FAMILY ownership (unownedUnlock=0), but the SHADE drifts ahead of the user repeatedly (calm__02 'settled', pressure__04 'stretched'+'guilt', pressure__08 'trapped', hurt__10 'disappointment') and tags it user_stated/user_confirmed. Because memory is now auto-learned at settled moments, the ledger can persist a shade the person never claimed, and that error compounds across sessions.
recommendations.change: Add a shade-level ownership check to labelIsUserOwned(): a shade may only be tagged user_stated/user_confirmed if that specific word (or a close stem) appears in the user's turns; otherwise downgrade the shade to companion_hypothesis even when the family is owned, and store the family + the user's own phrase rather than the inferred shade. In memoryLedger.ts, only auto-learn the shade when it passes this check; otherwise record the user's verbatim phrase. This keeps capture honest without blocking the unlock (family ownership still drives the gate).
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/stage.ts (labelIsUserOwned shade pass) and src/services/memoryLedger.ts (auto-learn guard).

recommendations.title: Raise the bar for unlocking on thin / flat material so a first shape never lands as a let-down
recommendations.problem: The First-Shape gate is well-tuned on average but trips on short or flat turns where users need more than one message to find a word: flat__07 unlocked at turn 3 on a one-line elaboration and the user openly protested ('thats it? i kind of expected more'); shame__04 unlocked turn 1 on surface 'irritated' before the real centre (shame) arrived. Both fail UNLOCK-SATISFACTION — the payoff the app exists to deliver.
recommendations.change: In evaluateStage(), add two conditions before 'understood' can fire: (a) require that the reflection carrying the unlock has enough specific, user-sourced material to read as a discovery (e.g. references a concrete user phrase/anchor beyond the bare label) rather than a one-line acknowledgement; and (b) for the flat/numb family and for very short user turns, require a second substantive user turn before unlock, since one rich message is rarely enough to find the word there. For shame specifically, suppress a turn-1 unlock on a surface irritation word when the opener is thin, to avoid locking a shape before the centre emerges.
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/stage.ts evaluateStage() (unlock richness threshold + family/turn-length-aware minimum).

recommendations.title: Extend the trailing-question guard to pre/post-unlock turns and double-barreled questions
recommendations.problem: dropTrailingQuestion() correctly protects the unlock turn (unlockEndedQ fell to 1), but REST is still breached on non-unlock turns: the companion appends a probing question after the user has begun to leave (hurt__06 after 'gonna try to sleep', hurt__05), and a few turns ask two things at once (pressure__08/__09 'more frozen, tight, or heavy?'). These nudge a gentle moment toward interrogation.
recommendations.change: Two targeted additions: (1) when the user's latest message contains a wind-down/exit cue ('gonna sleep', 'gotta go', 'thanks'), have the post-processing strip any trailing question on that turn too, not only at unlock — let it close on the reflection. (2) Add a single-question enforcement that collapses double-barreled questions ('X, or what does it make you want to do?') down to one. Keep this purely structural so it composes with the existing dropTrailingQuestion().
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/openaiClient.ts (generalize dropTrailingQuestion to exit-cue turns) and src/services/ai/responsePolicy.ts (one-question-per-turn enforcement).

recommendations.title: Make the reflection more tentative when the user is guarded/joking, and keep it to mirroring rather than naming inner mechanisms
recommendations.problem: The propose-tentatively rule holds in most places, but the companion occasionally reads a still-deflecting user a beat early (pressure__05 'shame with a self-critical edge' -> 'didnt come here to get read like that lol') or introduces a clinical-adjacent construct the user never raised (anger__09 'the anger is doing some defending... self-directed shame'). These stay just inside the no-advice line but trade the 'wait for them' contract for momentum.
recommendations.change: In prompts.ts, add a conditional softening rule: when the user's latest turn is joking, deflecting, or hedged ('lol', 'i guess', 'whatever'), the companion must use a visibly tentative frame ('I might be off, but...') and avoid naming a sharp self-evaluative quality until the user has reached for it. Reinforce the existing mirror rule with an explicit boundary: reflect the user's words and felt experience, do not name defence mechanisms, motives, or inner machinery the user did not state. This is a guidance change, not a new gate, so it stays within voice.
recommendations.where_in_code: src/services/ai/prompts.ts (NAME IT WITH THEM rule — add the guarded-user tentativeness clause and the no-inner-mechanism boundary).
